title: Project AI settings document v1
description: The guidance document of one project: the text every manual test case and generated script is written from. One shape validates the API `settings` member, the template `content` member and the input to `content_hash`, so the three cannot drift. Unknown members are refused at the document level and inside `priority_criteria`, so a typo is a 422 rather than silently stored content. Lengths are Unicode code points (RFC 8259 string length), the same unit as PostgreSQL `char_length` and the server's own counter. The four plan-13 limits are contractual: writing_style 250, coverage_strategy 1500, exclusion_rules 1500, step_detail 200; description 1000, environment_url 2048 and each criterion 250 are the recommended defaults recorded for the owner question on the remaining caps. `languages` is stored sorted ascending with no duplicates; a request naming a language twice is refused by the validator with `duplicate_value`, and the array bound here mirrors that rule. `environment_url` is an absolute http(s) URL without credentials: its scheme, userinfo and secret-shaped segments are checked by the shared URL rule at runtime, which a JSON Schema cannot express faithfully, so this schema bounds its length only.

description.description: What the project's AI-written cases should know first: the product area, its users and the flow under test.

environment_url.description: The application origin the guidance is written for, null when the project has not named one. Absolute http(s), no userinfo and no secret-shaped part, checked by the shared URL rule at runtime.

languages.description: The output languages of generated cases, stored sorted ascending ('en' before 'vi'). Closed to the two G1 locales: widening the set needs a migration, because the table's CHECK carries the same pair.

writing_style.description: How a step should read: voice, person, what to name and what to leave out (contractual cap: 250 code points).

coverage_strategy.description: What every checklist item must cover: the paths, boundaries, authorization cases and destructive actions the project expects (contractual cap: 1500 code points).

priority_criteria.description: One criterion per checklist priority level, so the same word means the same thing in every item of the project.

critical.description: What makes a failure critical: the release-blocking class of defect.

high.description: What makes a failure high: a wrong main path or a missing check that still has a workaround.

medium.description: What makes a failure medium: a secondary path, a validation message or an empty state.

low.description: What makes a failure low: wording, spacing or cosmetics that change no behaviour.

exclusion_rules.description: What must never be tested automatically, such as destructive actions against real customer data (contractual cap: 1500 code points).

step_detail.description: How much detail a single step carries (contractual cap: 200 code points).
